title: Can Carpet Be Installed Over a Squeaky Subfloor?
meta: Yes, carpet can go over a squeaky subfloor, but the squeak stays unless it is fixed first. How pros screw down and shim Snohomish subfloors. Wills Flooring.
keywords: carpet over squeaky subfloor, fix squeaky floor before carpet, squeaky subfloor under carpet, subfloor screws before carpet, how to stop floor squeaks carpet installation

blocks.lead: Yes, carpet can be installed over a squeaky subfloor, and it usually is. But carpet and pad only muffle a squeak, they do not stop it. The right time to fix it is the one day the old carpet is up and the plywood is bare.
blocks.detail: Most squeaks are plywood rubbing on a nail or a joist as it moves. The fix is screws into the joists, shims or adhesive at gaps, and a replaced sheet where the wood is soft. Skip it and you will hear the same squeak through the new carpet for fifteen years. Carpet labor is published, $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in and $30 per step; the subfloor work is scoped on top of that at the estimate.

blocks.html: Snohomish houses squeak. Farmhouses on Fobes Hill have hundred-year-old fir subfloors, 1970s houses toward Clearview have plywood nailed down before construction adhesive was standard, and almost everything sits over a crawlspace that swings from damp to dry. So when the bedroom carpet is finally getting replaced, the question is fair: deal with the squeak, or just put the new carpet down? You can install right over it. Whether you should is the rest of this post.

blocks.text: Why floors squeak in the first place

items.title: Nails that have let go
items.text: Plywood was nailed, the joists dried and shrank a fraction, and now the sheet lifts off the nail shank with every step and drops back. That rub is the classic squeak. Screws fix it; more nails do not.

items.title: Gaps between plywood and joist
items.text: A joist that is low or crowned leaves a void under the sheet, and the plywood flexes into it. Shims glued in from below, or adhesive injected from above, take the movement out.

items.title: Crawlspace moisture cycles
items.text: Snohomish crawlspaces run wet. Joists swell in winter and shrink in summer, so fasteners loosen a little every year. Squeaks that show up each August and fade by spring are moisture squeaks.

items.title: Soft or delaminated wood
items.text: A past leak under a bathroom or a long-term crawlspace vapor problem leaves plywood that crushes underfoot. That is not a squeak to screw down. The sheet gets cut out and replaced.

blocks.text: What a proper subfloor fix looks like on install day

items.text: Old carpet, pad and tack strip come up, and staples are pulled rather than hammered flat. With the plywood bare, every squeak can be found by walking it.
We mark every squeak with chalk, then find the joists with a stud finder or by the old nail lines. The fix is only permanent if the screw hits the joist.
Coarse-thread subfloor screws that bite 1 in or more into the joist, every 6 to 8 in through the squeaky area, heads sunk just below the surface so nothing telegraphs through the pad.
items.note: A typical bedroom takes 40 to 80 screws and about an hour.

items.text: Where the sheet still moves, adhesive is injected into the gap or a glued shim goes in from the crawlspace. Rubbing seams between sheets get a bead too.
Any sheet that flexes, smells musty or crumbles at the edge is cut out and replaced with plywood of the same thickness before the pad goes down.

blocks.text: Carpet over the squeak vs fixing it first

a.title: Worth the hour when
items: The squeak is in a bedroom, hallway or stairs you hear every night
The old carpet is already coming up, so the plywood is exposed anyway
The house is over a crawlspace and the squeaks change with the season
You are selling in the next few years; buyers walk floors and listen

b.title: Defensible when
items: The squeak is one spot in a closet or under a bed that never moves
The subfloor is old tongue-and-groove fir where screws help less
The room is a short-term rental turnover and the budget is the budget
The noise comes from joists or ductwork below, which carpet work cannot reach

blocks.title: The honest part:
blocks.text: Carpet with a thick, dense pad will make a squeak quieter. It will not make it go away, and the pad breaks down over the years while the squeak does not. If an installer tells you the new carpet will fix it, that is not true.

blocks.text: Mistakes that leave the squeak in place

items.html: Screwing between joists. A screw that misses the joist holds nothing. The squeak is quieter for a week and back by the next rainy season. Find the joist first.
Using drywall screws. They snap under floor loads. Subfloor screws are thicker and coarse-threaded for a reason.
Fixing only the marked spots. If one area has loose nails, the whole room does. Screw the whole traffic path, not three chalk marks.
Ignoring the crawlspace. Standing water, a torn vapor barrier or missing insulation under a Snohomish house will loosen the new screws too. The crawlspace is part of the floor.
Waiting until the carpet is down. Squeak repair kits that go through carpet leave holes in the new carpet and rarely reach a joist. The one cheap moment is between tear-out and install.

blocks.text: Before your carpet install: a subfloor checklist

items: Walk every room in socks and mark squeaks with tape so the crew knows where to look after tear-out
Note which squeaks are seasonal; those point to crawlspace moisture, which is worth a look before the new carpet goes down
Check the crawlspace for standing water, a torn vapor barrier or sagging insulation
Ask the installer whether subfloor screwing is included, how many screws per room, and whether they locate joists first
Confirm soft spots will be cut out and replaced rather than covered
If the squeak is on stairs, ask for the treads and risers to be screwed and glued from behind if there is access
Read how to prepare for carpet installation so furniture is out and the crew has the floor bare on day one

faq.q: Will new carpet and padding stop my floor from squeaking?
faq.a: No. Carpet and pad muffle the sound, and a dense pad can make it noticeably quieter, but the plywood is still moving against the nail or joist underneath. The squeak returns in full as the pad compresses. Screwing the subfloor to the joists is the only real fix.

faq.q: How do you fix a squeaky subfloor before carpet?
faq.a: With the old carpet and pad removed, the crew walks the room, marks squeaks, finds the joists, and drives coarse-thread subfloor screws every 6 to 8 in along the joist through the loose area. Gaps get construction adhesive or glued shims. Soft plywood is cut out and replaced.

faq.q: Why does my floor squeak more in summer?
faq.a: Crawlspace moisture. Joists and plywood absorb moisture through the wet Snohomish winter and dry out in summer, so fasteners loosen a little each cycle and the wood rubs. Fixing the vapor barrier and ventilation below slows it down; screws into the joists stop the movement.

faq.q: Can squeaks be fixed from the crawlspace instead?
faq.a: Some can. Gaps between joist and plywood can be shimmed and glued from below, and a loose joist-to-beam connection can be blocked. But fastening plywood to joists is far faster from above with the carpet out, which is why the carpet install day is the right time.

faq.q: Is a squeaky floor a sign of a structural problem?
faq.a: Usually not. Most squeaks are fasteners and normal wood movement. Sagging, bouncing that rattles dishes, soft spots, or a musty smell are different and should be looked at before any flooring goes down. We will tell you at the estimate if what we see is beyond a screw-down.
